idiom_name: injected lock object answering #synchronize (Mutex, Monitor, Concurrent::ReadWriteLock)
implementation_notes: In Ruby the policy collapses to any object that answers synchronize: Mutex#synchronize performs acquire and release around a block (Scoped Locking in one call), Monitor#synchronize is the re-entrant variant - Monitor tracks an owner and a re-entry count - and the concurrent-ruby gem adds Concurrent::ReadWriteLock with acquire_read_lock/acquire_write_lock for reader/writer policies. The component stores the strategy handed to its constructor and never names a concrete lock, so the abstract Lock class and the guard are replaced by one block-taking call; a plain Mutex is enough when the component has a single critical section and no re-entrant paths.
pitfalls: Thread::Mutex is not re-entrant - a second #lock or nested #synchronize from the same thread raises ThreadError, so components with intra-component calls need Monitor or an interface/implementation split.
The block form releases only when the block exits normally; Thread#raise or Timeout.timeout crossing the critical section can leave state inconsistent, so keep it small and exception-safe.
MRI's global VM lock means threads interleave only around blocking I/O: a coarse lock around I/O-bound work still serializes it, and locking around CPU-bound work buys no parallelism at all.
